title: Radiation - 123 school
heading: Radiation
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.q: Which three types of radiation are released in radioactive decay?
questions.a: Alpha radiation, beta radiation and gamma radiation

questions.q: What does an alpha particle consist of?
questions.a: Two protons and two neutrons (a helium nucleus)

questions.q: What does a beta particle (beta-minus) consist of?
questions.a: A fast electron

questions.q: What is gamma radiation?
questions.a: Electromagnetic radiation with a lot of energy

questions.q: Which material already stops alpha radiation?
questions.a: A sheet of paper

questions.q: Which material stops beta radiation?
questions.a: A thin aluminium plate

questions.q: Which material is suitable for shielding gamma radiation?
questions.a: Thick lead or concrete

questions.q: Which type of radiation is the most penetrating?
questions.a: Gamma radiation

questions.q: Which type of radiation has the greatest ionising effect?
questions.a: Alpha radiation

questions.q: What does ionising radiation mean?
questions.a: Radiation that can knock electrons out of atoms or molecules

questions.q: Which radiation is ionising?
questions.a: X-rays

questions.q: Which radiation has the most energy?
questions.a: Gamma radiation

questions.q: What is the unit of activity (number of decays per second)?
questions.a: Becquerel (Bq)

questions.q: What is the unit of radiation dose in the body (a measure of the damage caused by radiation)?
questions.a: Sievert (Sv)

questions.q: A radioactive source has an activity of 500 Bq. How many atomic nuclei decay per second?
questions.a: 1 Bq = 1 decay per second, so 500 per second

questions.q: What is the half-life?
questions.a: The time in which half of the radioactive nuclei have decayed

questions.q: 80 g of a radioactive substance is present. The half-life is 4.0 days. How many grams are left after 12 days?
questions.a: 12 days = 3 half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 g

questions.q: A source has an activity of 100 Bq. What is the activity after 3 half-lives?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. What percentage of an amount of C-14 is left after 11 460 years?
questions.a: 11 460 years = 2 half-lives: 100% → 50% → 25%

questions.q: 1/8 of a substance is left. How many half-lives have passed?
questions.a: 1/2 → 1/4 → 1/8: three half-lives

questions.q: Radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the atomic number of the daughter nucleus?
questions.a: An alpha particle has 2 protons: 88 − 2 = 86

questions.q: Radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the mass number of the daughter nucleus?
questions.a: An alpha particle has mass number 4: 226 − 4 = 222

questions.q: Carbon-14 (atomic number 6) decays by beta-minus decay to nitrogen (atomic number 7). What happens to the mass number?
questions.a: A neutron changes into a proton: the mass number stays the same, the atomic number goes up by 1

questions.q: What is background radiation?
questions.a: Radiation that is always present around us, for example from the ground and from space

questions.q: What is the difference between irradiation and contamination?
questions.a: In irradiation you are hit by radiation from outside; in contamination there is radioactive material on or in your body

questions.q: How do you reduce the radiation exposure from a radioactive source? Name the three ways.
questions.a: Increase the distance, use a shorter time, use shielding

questions.q: What do you use to measure radioactive radiation?
questions.a: A Geiger counter

questions.q: What do you use X-rays for in a hospital?
questions.a: To make images of bones and organs

questions.q: Why is nuclear waste dangerous for a long time?
questions.a: Some substances have a very long half-life and so keep emitting radiation for a long time

questions.q: What happens in nuclear fission?
questions.a: A heavy atomic nucleus splits into smaller nuclei and energy is released

questions.q: Which radiation does a microwave oven use?
questions.a: Microwaves

questions.q: A smoke detector often contains a small source that emits alpha radiation. Why is that not dangerous as long as the detector is intact?
questions.a: Alpha radiation is already stopped by the casing and a thin layer of air

questions.q: Why is an alpha source especially dangerous if the radioactive material gets inside your body?
questions.a: Alpha radiation is strongly ionising and is completely absorbed in the body

questions.q: Name two applications of radioactive radiation.
questions.a: For example medical imaging (tracer), irradiation of tumours, sterilisation of medical equipment or preserving food

questions.q: What is the difference between ionising and non-ionising radiation? Give an example of each.
questions.a: Ionising radiation can ionise atoms (for example X-rays or gamma radiation); non-ionising radiation cannot (for example radio waves or visible light)
